description:
## Why
After fz-xxd.7, `@type t :: opaque U` is a brand over `U`: its values are `U`'s values, and a `@spec` position `t` rejects a bare `U`. Nothing yet stops a module other than the owner from reading the structure (`h.value`, `h[k]`, a structural pattern). Elixir's compiler does not check this either; Dialyzer does (`../elixir` 759443e72, `pages/references/typespecs.md:241`: "the internal structure of the type will not be visible").

## What changes
- A brand tag records whether it came from `refines` (structure visible) or `opaque` (structure hidden). This is fixed when the tag is minted, because a name's facts live in the symbol and nothing about a name is looked up.
- Every structural access (field, index, structural pattern) whose receiver carries an opaque tag owned by another module gets a diagnostic, under a new code in src/diag/codes.rs.
- fz-xxd.7 deletes the dead `check_opaque_visibility` / `src/types/visibility.rs`. This is built fresh at the access seam, not restored from them.

## Done when
A fixture reading `.value` of another module's opaque type fails with the new code on every path. 00431 (reads inside the owner) stays clean. The docs (set-theoretic-types.md, type-naming.md, guides) describe the rule.
title: An opaque type's structure is hidden outside its declaring module
